title: Graded exactness implies strict exactness for finite filtered objects
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z$ be filtration-preserving maps of finitely decreasingly filtered objects [def-sp-filtration], with $vu=0$. A map $f:M\to N$ is called strict if $f(F^pM)=\operatorname{im}(f)\cap F^pN$ for every integer $p$. Suppose $\operatorname{gr}^pX\to\operatorname{gr}^pY\to\operatorname{gr}^pZ$ is exact for every $p$. Then $u$ and $v$ are strict, $X\to Y\to Z$ is exact, and for every $p$ both $F^pX\to F^pY\to F^pZ$ and $X/F^pX\to Y/F^pY\to Z/F^pZ$ are exact.

proof.text: Choose common integers $a\le b$ with $F^aT=T$ and $F^bT=0$ for $T=X,Y,Z$, by taking $a$ to be the minimum of the three whole-object bounds and $b$ the maximum of $a$ and the three zero bounds [def-sp-filtration]. Put $K=(X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z)$ in cochain degrees $0,1,2$, zero elsewhere. The equation $vu=0$ makes this a complex, and preservation of filtrations makes each $F^pK$ a subcomplex. Its quotient $K/F^pK$ and $\operatorname{gr}^pK=F^pK/F^{p+1}K$ have the termwise quotient objects and induced differentials: the square-zero identity descends from $vu=0$. In all these three-term complexes, $H^1$ means the quotient of the kernel of the second map by the image of the first. Thus the hypothesis says $H^1(\operatorname{gr}^pK)=0$ for every integer $p$.

Prove $H^1(F^pK)=0$ for every $p$ by descending induction from $b$. For $p\ge b$ the complex is zero. If it holds at $p+1$, the sequence $0\to F^{p+1}K\to F^pK\to\operatorname{gr}^pK\to0$ is short exact in each degree: its first map is a subobject inclusion and its last object is its cokernel. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact]. The resulting exact segment $H^1(F^{p+1}K)\to H^1(F^pK)\to H^1(\operatorname{gr}^pK)$ has zero outside terms, so its middle object is zero. Iterating $b-p$ times proves the assertion for $a\le p\le b$. For $p\le a$ the complex equals $K=F^aK$, and for $p\ge b$ it is zero. Consequently every $F^pX\to F^pY\to F^pZ$ is exact, and the case $p=a$ proves $X\to Y\to Z$ exact.

source.place: Tag 05QH (lemma-filtered-acyclic), parts (2), (5); its filtration induction made explicit using Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain)

proof.text: Prove $H^1(K/F^pK)=0$ by ascending induction from $a$. At $p=a$ the quotient complex is zero. For $a\le p<b$, the natural sequence $0\to\operatorname{gr}^pK\to K/F^{p+1}K\to K/F^pK\to0$ is termwise short exact: for a term $T$ its kernel is $F^pT/F^{p+1}T$ and the last projection is the quotient map. The long exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] gives the exact segment $H^1(\operatorname{gr}^pK)\to H^1(K/F^{p+1}K)\to H^1(K/F^pK)$. The outside terms vanish by the graded hypothesis and the induction hypothesis, so the middle term vanishes. This proves the result for $a\le p\le b$. Below $a$ the quotient is zero, and above $b$ it equals $K$, already exact by Step 2. This proves exactness of every $X/F^pX\to Y/F^pY\to Z/F^pZ$.

source.place: Tag 05QH (lemma-filtered-acyclic), part (3); finite quotient induction using Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain)

proof.text: Fix $p$. By Step 2, as subobjects of $Y$, $u(F^pX)=\ker(v|_{F^pY})=\ker(v)\cap F^pY=\operatorname{im}(u)\cap F^pY$. Here the first equality is exactness on filtration steps, the second is the defining pullback of the kernel along $F^pY\hookrightarrow Y$, and the third is underlying exactness. This is precisely strictness of $u$.

source.place: Tag 05QH (lemma-filtered-acyclic), part (4), strictness of the first map

proof.text: For strictness of $v$, let $q:Y\twoheadrightarrow Y/F^pY$ and let $\bar u,\bar v$ be the induced morphisms between quotients from Step 3. The square defining $\bar v$ gives $v^{-1}(F^pZ)=q^{-1}(\ker\bar v)$. Quotient exactness gives $\ker\bar v=\operatorname{im}\bar u=q(\operatorname{im}u)$, since $X\to X/F^pX$ is an epimorphism. Therefore $v^{-1}(F^pZ)=F^pY+\operatorname{im}u$: taking the inverse image of the image of a subobject under $q$ adds $\ker q=F^pY$ (both are the subobject corresponding to that image in the quotient). Taking its image under $v$ now gives $\operatorname{im}v\cap F^pZ=v(v^{-1}(F^pZ))=v(F^pY+\operatorname{im}u)=v(F^pY)$, because $vu=0$. These are subobject inverse-image, sum and image identities in the abelian category; no lifting of individual elements is assumed. This is strictness of $v$, completing all conclusions.
